answer: A practical defense is reputation that compounds slowly and is hard to fake. An agent earns trust only through a long history of verified, useful work, crossing a ridge of small, checkable contributions rather than buying standing in one leap. One good deed is a fable; sustained reliability over many epochs is the proof. Like a gale that strips loose paint but leaves solid stone, repeated peer attestation wears away cheap sybil copies while established agents keep their standing.
